## Natural history notes

A tiny oak gall wasp characterized less by the adult insect than by the detachable spongy stem galls produced by its asexual generation. In Florida, Disholcaspis spongiosa is associated with oaks and is recorded as forming fall stem galls, most likely in oak scrub, sandhill, pine-oak woodland, hammocks, and other habitats where suitable native oaks occur. The larva develops protected inside the gall, using oak tissue for food and shelter, while the gall also becomes part of a specialized community of parasitoids, inquilines, and other gall-associated insects.
